the_actual_retained_delivery_path.a_discovery_preflight_still_passes_thoug: http_lake.discover() swallows 'lake unreachable' and returns an empty list, and describe() and storage() degrade to placeholders.  The last event on this lake is a 2026-09-27 discover recorded as ALLOW while the unit was already down.  coverage, read and download do not swallow.  A consumer that preflights with discover alone will believe the lake is healthy and then fail at its first byte
the_actual_retained_delivery_path.a_warm_cache_does_NOT_avoid_the_endpoint: tools/governed_run.py governed_download issues a real GET to the kernel's /api/v2/download on every unit and re-streams and re-verifies the body; the `cached` flag only says the content-addressed target already existed.  data-gov's http_lake proxies that read to the lake's own base_url.  So while the unit is down, every household consumer is refused at the download step, warm cache or not.  The endpoint is a hard prerequisite, not an optimisation
